messages:
maria: Heads up — partner webhook accidentally logged a staging config last night. It contains a KMS ciphertext for the staging DB password and an old service-account key blob. Not an immediate prod outage but we need a coordinated scrub + rotation. Proposed steps: revoke SA key, rotate DB creds, rewrap ciphertext with a new KMS key, tighten Vault RBAC on partner paths, and enable immediate audit forwarding to Splunk. Who can own the playbook and first steps?
jonathan: I’m on-call today, I can own the SA key revoke + creating a replacement key. Which key ID is it?
maria: Key id: 0a9b8c7d-psa (from svc-partner@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com). It’s the one referenced in the webhook payload.
jonathan: Got it. I’ll revoke now. Command I’ll run:
```
gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete 0a9b8c7d-psa --iam-account=svc-partner@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```
shiv: Quick note on the KMS ciphertext: because partner logs contained the ciphertext blob (not plaintext), we should rewrap instead of forcing a DB/secret rotation immediately if the ciphertext is still bound to our KMS key. Rewrap flow: decrypt with the old key (offline, secops VM), then encrypt with new key/version. Steps I usually run:
```
gcloud kms decrypt --location=global --keyring=rw-keyring --key=old-stage-key --ciphertext-file=blob.ct --plaintext-file=blob.plain
gcloud kms encrypt --location=global --keyring=rw-keyring --key=new-stage-key --plaintext-file=blob.plain --ciphertext-file=blob.rewrapped
```
shiv: Important: do the decrypt on an ephemeral, locked-down host and remove blob.plain after re-encrypt.
alice: I’ll take Vault RBAC. We should deny partner read access to /secret/data/partner/* and only allow write-for-ingest if needed. I’ll apply a short-term restrictive policy and then add exceptions if it breaks ingestion. Example policy snippet I’ll apply: 
```
path "secret/data/partner/*" {
  capabilities = ["create","update"]
}
path "secret/data/partner/*" {
  capabilities = ["read"]
  allowed_parameters = { "allowed_entities" = [] }
  # effectively deny read by default
}
```
alice: Also will push a change to the Vault auditing config to ensure all accesses on that path are forwarded to Splunk (no sampling).
vault-bot: Audit device 'splunk-audit' enabled on mount 'audit/' with forwarding to https://splunk.redwood.corp (sample-id: splk-1147).
oncall-sre: Scheduling note — revoke/rotation should be done with a canary and a short maintenance window for partner integrations (15-30m). If partner services poll frequently, we might cause retries. Recommend notify partner slack and set a 1-hour window for key swap. I can coordinate notifications.
maria: Proposed timeline: revoke SA key now (jonathan). Create replacement SA key and hand to partner in secure channel within 30m. Rewrap KMS ciphertext within 2 hours (shiv). Vault RBAC restriction in 30m (alice) as a short-term lock. Audit forwarding immediate (alice). Post changes, run canary and monitor error spike for 2 hours.
jonathan: Revoke done — returned 200 and key removed from IAM. I’ve created new key and uploaded it to a secure artifact for partner pickup. Command I used to create: 
```
gcloud iam service-accounts keys create new-key.json --iam-account=svc-partner@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```
jonathan: I did not paste the key anywhere public — new-key.json is in gs://redwood-secops/keys/ENC-ACCESS and ACLed to seceng-only. I messaged partner through their secure onboarding channel for coordinated rollout.
shiv: I performed decrypt on the locked secops VM and re-encrypted with the new-stage-key. Uploaded rewrapped blob to s3://redwood-secops/rewraps/staging-blob.rewrapped. I ran a quick sanity decrypt with the new key in a staging node and verified the plaintext matches expected DB user. Script used is in the private repo secops/rewrap-scripts (internal).
alice: Applied Vault policy to restrict partner read on /secret/data/partner/* and enabled audit forwarding. I added an exception for seceng-bot to read for validation. Will monitor for failures and roll back if ingestion breaks.
vault-bot: Policy 'partner-tight-read' created by alice at 2026-03-21T14:45:00Z.
oncall-sre: I created incident INC-2026-214 and scheduled a 60-minute post-mortem check-in at +24h. Pagerduty alerting configured for any Vault audit spikes.
maria: Thanks all. Action items summarized: jonathan = SA revoke + new key handoff (done); shiv = rewrap + upload (done); alice = Vault RBAC + audit forwarding (done); oncall-sre = incident ticket + partner notification. Please PR the short playbook to infra-runbooks referencing this thread (tag: eng-security) and attach the minimal commands we ran.
jonathan: PR opened: https://git.redwood.internal/infra-runbooks/pulls/48 — contains revoke/create steps and notes on secure key delivery.
shiv: Note for postmortem: ask partner to check their webhook log retention settings — they had full body logging enabled. Recommend partner turn on redaction and rotate their ingest role.
alice: I’ll follow up with IAM team about long-term Vault RBAC changes (least-privilege onboarding flow).
maria: Closing the triage here for now — reopen if we see audit spikes or partner reports issues. :thumbsup:
jonathan: :thumbsup:
shiv: :+1:
alice: Thanks everyone.
